messages.author: f8f4b040f036a918
messages.subject: Understanding SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat
parts:
Dear MSstats Team, 

I was wondering if there is a way to check the impact of each filtering step on the input data during the conversion to MSstats format using SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat.

I am trying to understand how the data is transformed in each step of the conversion in an attempt to try understand how the final data is reported. 

I had a look at the source code for the SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat and this was helpful to understand the base of the function. However I was just wondering if it maybe possible to see the results of each filtering parameter to help understand how the data is transforming along the way. 

I look forward to hearing your suggestions. 


Kind regards

Suniya

messages.author: 5c6e92c10ef28984
messages.subject: Re: Understanding SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat
parts:
Hi,


almost. Most a lot of the steps can be run separately by using the extended workflow (MSstatsXYZ functions: MSstatsClean -> MSstatsPreprocess and so on). For operations that are done within the same function, you can take the output of the previous step in the workflow and calculate summary statistics. For example, before running MSstatsPreprocess with options "remove proteins with a single feature" and "remove shared peptides", calculate the number of shared peptides and proteins that only have a single feature. Otherwise, there is no way see the details, but inspecting the log file may help, too. We might consider producing output with additional details in the future, but it won't happen in the nearest future.
What information is of particular interest? (=which filtering/aggregation steps)

Kind regards,
Mateusz

messages.author: 6597c45f2a31b5d0
messages.subject: Re: Understanding SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat
parts:
Hi Suniya,

Looking into your inquiry, I think the best approach to understand what is happening in the function is to use the `trace` function.  With this function, you can walk through each step of the function and analyze how the data looks at each step.  This is generally what I do when I'm trying to understand what's happening within a function for any package.  Here's an example of using it below:

```
trace(MSstatsPTM::SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat, browser) # add SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat as a function to dive into step by step
SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat(input) # Run the function
```

Thanks,
Tony
